Linux:bombuzal.d: Bombuzal, known in America as Ka-Blooey, is a 1988 puzzle video game designed by Antony Crowther (credited as "Ratt" in the game) and David Bishop for Image Works. The game was initially released in 1988 for the Amiga, Atari ST and Commodore 64. It was later released in 1989 for MS-DOS. It was released for Nintendo Entertainment System consoles not long after — in December 1990 in Japan for the Super Famicom, and in August 1992 in North America (where it was named as Ka-Blooey). The game has a sequel/remake available for the Nintendo 64 called Charlie Blast's Territory.

Apple2:airheart.d: Airheart is an action game designed and programmed by Dan Gorlin for the Apple II and published by Broderbund in 1986. It requires a 128K Apple IIe (or later) to run, as it uses the 16-color double hi-res graphics mode. After three years of development, the game was technically advanced at its time of release, using scaled sprites for 3D effects, but did not include all of the planned features. Gorlin reworked the game as Typhoon Thompson in Search for the Sea Child for the Atari ST (1988), and later the Amiga (1990), which is closer to what he originally envisioned.
